name: cps converter
seoDesc: cps converter: work out frequency in cycles per second from the frequency in hertz. A free conversion calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The cps converter returns frequency in cycles per second from the 1 field on the form. No sign-up, no page reload, and the relationship behind it is printed below. Think of it as a shortcut for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the cps converter calculator work?
sections.html:
The cps converter takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports frequency in cycles per second in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the frequency in hertz.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in hertz. The unit chip switches it to any of the 21 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the cps converter calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Frequency in cycles per second=frequency in hertz
Frequency in cycles per second=frequency in kilohertz
Frequency in cycles per second=frequency in megahertz
Frequency in cycles per second=frequency in radians per second
Frequency in cycles per second=frequency in degrees per second
Frequency in cycles per minute=frequency in cycles per second

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Frequency, opening in cycles per second
  • Frequency, opening in cycles per minute
  • Frequency, opening in revolutions per minute
  • Frequency, opening in hertz
  • Frequency, opening in kilohertz
  • Frequency, opening in megahertz
  • Frequency, opening in gigahertz
  • Frequency, opening in degrees per second

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The cps converter earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Converting a figure someone quoted you so you can compare it
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values
  • Reading a recipe written in units you do not use
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the frequency in hertz — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the cps converter calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns frequency in cycles per second, derived from the frequency in hertz. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the cps converter calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the frequency in hertz, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter frequency in cycles per second in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Frequency in cycles per second opens in cycles per second and the chip beside it offers 21 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the cps converter calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
